\chapter{Synthesis --- The Conversation Without Them}
\label{ch:synthesis-without-repeating}
\hlchaptermodality{92}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can carry a four-turn exchange using pronouns, and say what a pronoun promises the listener.}

Complete ES-C45-sintesis-sin-repetir: run the exchange with pronouns and say what goes wrong when the gender points at nothing.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{Synthesis — the conversation without them}

\label{lesson:ES-C45-sintesis-sin-repetir}



\begin{quote}
\emph{¿Tienes los libros?} Answer yes without saying \emph{libros}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{The exchange}
Four turns, with the pronouns:

\begin{quote}
— \emph{¿Tienes los libros?} — \emph{Sí, los tengo.} — \emph{¿Y las comidas?} — \emph{Las hago hoy.}
\end{quote}

Now the same four turns without them:

\begin{quote}
— \emph{¿Tienes los libros?} — \emph{Sí, tengo los libros.} — \emph{¿Y las comidas?} — \emph{Hago las comidas hoy.}
\end{quote}

Read the second version aloud, all four lines. It is not wrong anywhere. It is exhausting, and by the fourth line it sounds like somebody being careful with a stranger rather than talking.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: what a pronoun buys, and what it costs}]
The pronoun buys speed, and it is paid for with \textbf{attention}.

\emph{Los tengo} is only clear because both of you remember what \emph{los} points at. If the last three sentences were about meals and you say \emph{los tengo}, your listener hunts for a masculine thing and finds none. A pronoun is a promise that the thing is still in the room.

That is the real skill, and it is not on the grid: \textbf{hold what has been said, and point back at it accurately.} English asks the same of you and you have done it since you were three, which is why nobody taught it to you. Here the pointer must also agree in gender and number — which is why \emph{lo} and \emph{la} were the hard quarter of that table.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item both versions of the four-turn exchange, and hear the second one tire
  \item \textquotedblleft{}los tengo\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}las hago\textquotedblright{} until the gender arrives with the noun, not after it
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\emph{¿Tienes los libros?} (\emph{\textbf{Sí, los tengo}}.) \emph{¿Y las comidas?} (\emph{\textbf{Las hago}}.) What does a pronoun promise? (That the thing it points at is \textbf{still in the room}.) Next: the past tense.
\end{tcolorbox}
